title: Scientists are finding AI may make us remember things that never happened
source_used: Metro (relaying The Washington Post; WaPo blocked, HTTP 000)
key_facts: Metro, citing the Washington Post, says scientists think AI may be messing with human memory and judgment.
Metro says AI-generated images and fake news can leave people confident that events happened when they did not.
Pattie Maes of the MIT Media Lab ran an experiment with 54 people writing essays: no tools, Google without AI answers, or ChatGPT.
Metro says the no-tools group had the strongest brain connectivity and the ChatGPT group the weakest and could not recall their own words later.
Gideon Nave of the University of Pennsylvania: 'If you don't use it, you lose it.'
quote_evidence: Scientists have found that artificial intelligence may be messing with our brains more than we realise.
Those who were allowed to use AI, however, showed the weakest connectivity and couldn’t recall their own words when asked to later.
why_it_matters_hint: Heavy AI use may weaken recall and judgment, according to the researchers quoted.
notes: Washington Post is blocked and paywalled; only Metro's rewrite was read, so the entry stays headline-level. The MIT experiment is described in Metro as the basis; its date is not given.
